title: Opening any saved conversation is a hard server error: /chat/[conversationId] is a Server Component that calls the client-only apiFetch
evidence: The file has no "use client" and is an `async` Server Component. Line 6: `const { messages } = await getConversationMessages(conversationId);` → frontend/app/lib/api.ts:53 → api.ts:41 `apiFetch` → frontend/app/lib/auth-client.ts:1 which IS `"use client"`. Compiled proof from the committed build, frontend/.next/server/chunks/ssr/_0e1pju2._.js: the page module is `async function f({params:a}){...await d(`/api/v1/conversations/${c}/messages`)...}` where `d` calls `c.apiFetch`, and in that same server graph `apiFetch` is `registerClientReference(function(){throw Error("Attempted to call apiFetch() from the server but apiFetch is on the client...")},"[project]/frontend/app/lib/auth-client.ts","apiFetch")`. The codebase already diagnosed and fixed this exact pattern elsewhere: frontend/app/agent/[id]/page.tsx:7-17 says "As a server component this page ran getTask(id) during the server render ... Neither exists on the server, so the render threw before the page ever reached the browser: the route was a hard error" — /agent/[id] and /coding/[id] were converted, /chat/[conversationId] was missed. There is also no error.tsx/global-error.tsx anywhere under frontend/app (find returned nothing), so the user gets Next's raw error screen.
impact: Every click on a conversation in the chat sidebar (ChatView.tsx:87-94) 500s. Worse, the FIRST message of a new chat also lands there: ChatView.tsx:69-73 does `router.replace(`/chat/${result.value}`)` as soon as the stream finishes, so a brand-new user's very first chat turn ends on an error page even though the answer streamed correctly. Chat history is unreachable for everyone.
fix: Convert it to a client page exactly like frontend/app/agent/[id]/page.tsx: `"use client"`, `const { conversationId } = use(params)`, and load messages inside ChatView (or a client loader modelled on frontend/app/agent/task-detail-loader.tsx) so apiFetch runs in the browser with the cookie, CSRF token and project id.

title: A chat send against an unreachable API fails silently — empty assistant bubble, no error, unhandled rejection
evidence: ChatView.tsx:50-76 is `try { ...stream... } finally { setIsStreaming(false) }` with NO `catch`. streamChat only converts an HTTP error response into an `error` event (chat-stream.ts:85-95); a transport-level rejection from `fetch` (chat-stream.ts:77) escapes the generator. I ran a temporary probe (frontend/app/chat/__probe_chatview_1.test.ts, since deleted) that stubbed fetch to throw TypeError("Failed to fetch") on POST /api/v1/chat. Vitest output: `Unhandled Rejection TypeError: Failed to fetch ❯ streamChat app/lib/chat-stream.ts:77:21 ❯ handleSubmit app/chat/ChatView.tsx:58:33`, and the rendered state was `{ assistant: '', errorBubbles: 0, errorText: null }` — an empty assistant bubble and nothing else.
impact: The single most likely local condition (API not started, wrong NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL, CORS refusal) makes the user's message vanish into a blank bubble with no explanation anywhere in the UI. The failure is visible only in the browser console.
fix: Add a `catch` around the stream loop in handleSubmit that replaces the trailing assistant bubble with `{ content: String(err), isError: true }`, the same shape the `error` event path already uses at ChatView.tsx:64-66.

title: No audio/TTS screen exists at all — the required AUDIO generation journey has no UI, no nav entry and no API client call
evidence: NAV_LINKS (app-chrome.tsx:7-21) lists Chat, Tasks, Images, Videos, Files, Ask, Memory, Usage, Platform, Settings — no Audio. There is no frontend/app/audio directory (directory listing of frontend/app). frontend/app/lib/api.ts has no speech/TTS function. Grep of every `"/api/v1` literal in backend/src (excluding tests) returns no audio or speech route; speech synthesis exists only as an internal library, backend/packages/media/src/speech.ts, used by the video scene pipeline. The only place synthesised audio is ever playable is the per-scene `<audio>` inside a video project (frontend/app/videos/[id]/page.tsx:116).
impact: The owner's bar requires TTS generation from the UI with a Linux-capable provider. A user cannot generate any audio from the application at all — only as an invisible side effect of a long-form video.
fix: Add frontend/app/audio/page.tsx (prompt/text + voice select, submit, poll, `<audio controls src={assetUrl(...)}>`) plus a nav entry, over a new backend POST/GET /api/v1/audio that wraps backend/packages/media/src/speech.ts the way images.ts wraps the image provider. The machine already has piper TTS verified working and it ships Linux builds, so no credential is missing.

title: Model-driven tool calling is unreachable from chat: the client never sends `tools` and never renders a tool_call event
evidence: chat-stream.ts:81 sends `body: JSON.stringify({ messages, conversationId })` — no `tools`, no `toolChoice`, although shared/src/chat.ts:55-56 defines both on chatRequestSchema and backend/src/routes/v1/chat.ts:376 spreads the whole request into the router. backend/packages/model-router/src/router.ts:141 shows tool capability is decided purely by `request.tools?.length` — there is no server-side default tool injection (grep for "tools" in chat.ts returns only line 413, a comment). On the receive side, ChatView.tsx:61-66 handles only `token` and `error`; `tool_call` and `done` events are discarded, even though frontend/app/lib/chat-stream.test.ts has a test literally named "yields tool_call events so the UI can show what the agent is doing".
impact: In the chat screen the model is never offered a tool, so it can never call one; and if a tool call did arrive it would render as nothing. The only tool calling a user can trigger is a fixed agent-task recipe on /tasks. The `done` event's provider/model/usage are also dropped, so chat never says which model answered.
fix: Fetch the project's enabled tools from GET /api/v1/tools, pass them as `tools` on the chat POST, and render `tool_call` events (name + arguments) and the `done` event's provider/model in the transcript.

title: The autonomous multi-step agent cannot be started from the UI — the task-type list omits it
evidence: TASK_TYPES at tasks/page.tsx:9-16 offers echo_chat, read_and_summarize, mcp_read_and_summarize, delete_sandbox_file, fix_failing_test, answer_from_documents. shared/src/task-graph.ts:145-160 defines a seventh, `autonomous`: "the open-ended type: no fixed plan, no hardcoded steps. The model receives the goal and the tools it is allowed to use and drives the task itself (ADR-064)". Its planner needs `input.goal` (backend/packages/agent-core/src/planner.ts:90-92) and its budgets live in backend/packages/agent-core/src/reasoning-loop.ts:103 (`maxIterations: 12, maxTotalTokens: 200_000`). No frontend file references "autonomous" or "goal".
impact: The only genuinely multi-step, model-driven agent — the one that carries the iteration and token budgets the owner requires — is reachable only by curl. Every agent run a user can start from the app is a deterministic hardcoded recipe. Additionally frontend/app/agent/TaskDetail.tsx:106 has no branch for `kind === "reasoning"`, so such a node would render as a bare "Model call" with none of its iterations or tool calls shown.
fix: Add `{ value: "autonomous", label: "Autonomous agent (model-driven)", fields: ["goal"] }` to TASK_TYPES, optionally expose maxIterations/maxTotalTokens as inputs, and add a `reasoning` branch to TaskDetail.tsx:106 that renders the run's transcript/toolCallCount/stopReason from the node output.

title: Chat has no stop control — the AbortController is created and never aborted, so the backend's cancellation path is unreachable
evidence: ChatView.tsx:48 `const controller = new AbortController();` — the signal is passed to streamChat (line 54) but `controller.abort()` is never called. Grep across frontend/app for `abort|AbortController` (excluding tests) returns exactly two hits: ChatView.tsx:48 and a comment at chat-stream.ts:126. There is no Stop button in the composer (ChatView.tsx:112-122). The server side is fully built for it: backend/src/routes/v1/chat.ts:298-320 explains the disconnect handling and chat.ts:395-400 says "break ... the difference between 'we ignore the rest' and 'we are no longer billed for the rest'".
impact: A user who asks for something long cannot stop it; tokens keep being spent until the model finishes or they close the tab. Cancellation is one of the owner's named requirements and its client half does not exist.
fix: Hold the controller in a ref, render a Stop button while `isStreaming`, call `controller.abort()` on click, and treat the resulting AbortError as a normal end-of-turn rather than an error.

title: Enabling a disabled-by-default (MCP) tool is impossible from the app, and the Tasks screen instructs users to call an endpoint that 404s for them
evidence: The Platform Tools table (platform/page.tsx:230-262) renders id/enabled/risk/approval with no action column — no enable or disable control anywhere in the frontend (grep for `tools/` + `enable` in frontend returns nothing). Meanwhile tasks/page.tsx:100-106 tells the user: "enable it first via POST /api/v1/tools/mcp.reference-filesystem.read_text_file/enable". That route is system-admin only — backend/src/routes/v1/platform.ts:114-116 calls `requireSystemAdmin(request)`, which throws NotFoundError for a non-admin (platform.ts:245-249) — and self-signup never grants that flag: backend/packages/security/src/auth-service.ts:98 `signup` passes `isSystemAdmin: false`, with auth-service.ts:129 `bootstrapSystemAdmin` the only other path, gated on an empty user table.
impact: A user who signs up through the UI can never enable an MCP tool. Selecting "Read & summarize (via MCP)" on the Tasks screen always fails with "tool disabled", and the on-screen remedy is unusable for that user — a dead instruction on a required capability.
fix: Add an enable/disable button to the Platform Tools table (rendered only when `user.isSystemAdmin`), and make the Tasks note conditional: tell a non-admin that a system administrator must enable it rather than handing them a request that will 404.

title: MCP connection errors are never displayed: the Platform screen reads `server.error`, the API sends `lastError`
evidence: McpRow declares `error?: string | null` (platform/page.tsx:42) and the row renders `{server.error ? {server.error} : null}` (platform/page.tsx:224). The route sends no `error` field: backend/src/routes/v1/platform.ts:124-141 returns `{ id, status, transport, toolCount, toolIds, refusedToolIds, lastError, connectedAt }`. `server.error` is therefore always undefined. `transport` and `refusedToolIds` are also dropped, although platform.ts:131-134 states refusedToolIds must be "Shown, not just logged: on a remote server that is what a name-squatting attempt looks like, and a boot-time log line is not where anyone goes looking for it."
impact: An MCP server that failed to connect shows only a status word with no reason, and a remote server attempting to squat an existing tool id is invisible in the only screen built to show it.
fix: Rename the field to `lastError` in McpRow and the JSX, and render `transport` and `refusedToolIds` alongside it.

title: Queue operations that exist in the API have no controls: no job cancel, no MCP reconnect
evidence: The Jobs table (platform/page.tsx:264-288) has columns Queue/State/Retries/Error and no action, although POST /api/v1/jobs/:queue/:id/cancel exists at backend/src/routes/v1/platform.ts:178-182. The MCP list (platform/page.tsx:215-228) has no control, although POST /api/v1/mcp/:id/reconnect exists at platform.ts:144-150. Only dead-letter replay is wired (platform/page.tsx:140-152).
impact: A stuck or runaway job cannot be cancelled from the operations screen, and a dropped MCP connection cannot be restarted — both are named parts of the queues and MCP requirements.
fix: Add a Cancel button per job row and a Reconnect button per MCP server, mirroring the existing `replay` handler; gate reconnect on `user.isSystemAdmin` since platform.ts:144 requires it.

title: The audit log and admin metrics/stats have no screen
evidence: The Platform loader fetches models, tools, mcp, jobs, dead-letter and admin/health (platform/page.tsx:95-102). No frontend file calls /api/v1/audit (backend/src/routes/v1/auth.ts:287), /api/v1/admin/metrics (platform.ts:271) or /api/v1/admin/stats (platform.ts:281).
impact: The security audit trail — who approved a tool call, who revoked a key — is invisible in the product, and the Prometheus exposition and platform stats that back the observability requirement have no consumer in the UI.
fix: Add an Audit section to Settings or Platform over GET /api/v1/audit (project:admin), and an admin-only Stats block over GET /api/v1/admin/stats.

title: Ingested documents cannot be deleted from the UI, so a removed file keeps feeding RAG answers
evidence: The document list (files/page.tsx:102-123) renders filename, source, scan status and status with no action control. frontend/app/lib/api.ts exposes listFiles, ingestFile, getFile, uploadFile (api.ts:163-188) and no delete. The endpoint exists and is documented as an audit fix: backend/src/routes/v1/rag.ts:246-255, whose comment says the chunk delete is "the half a user would actually notice ... leaving those behind would mean a 'deleted' document kept being quoted back into answers".
impact: A user who uploads the wrong document — or sensitive content — has no way to remove it, and it keeps being retrieved and cited on the Ask screen.
fix: Add `deleteFile` to lib/api.ts and a Delete button per row in files/page.tsx, then refresh the list.

title: Account deletion and project member management are implemented server-side but have no UI
evidence: The Settings screen offers account display + sign out (settings/page.tsx:54-65), project list/create (94-176), API keys (178-312) and a link to Memory (80-89). It never calls DELETE /api/v1/auth/account (backend/src/routes/v1/auth.ts:155, described there as self-service specifically because "a privacy requirement satisfied only by asking someone else is not satisfied") nor POST /api/v1/projects/:projectId/members (auth.ts:127).
impact: The self-service deletion the backend built for NFR-008 is unreachable, so in practice it is an operator ticket again; and a project can never gain a second member, which makes the multi-member RBAC model untestable from the product.
fix: Add a danger-zone card (current password + typed confirmation, matching the endpoint's three guards) and an 'Invite member' form (email + role) to Settings.

title: Approve, reject, cancel and video retry swallow their errors — a failed action looks like a successful one
evidence: handleApprove (TaskDetail.tsx:33-40) and handleReject (42-49) are try/finally with no catch; handleCancel (51-53) has no try at all — a rejected `cancelTask` becomes an unhandled promise rejection. Same shape at frontend/app/videos/[id]/page.tsx:29-37 (handleRetry, try/finally, no catch). None of these screens has an error state for an action failure, unlike the same file's node-error card at TaskDetail.tsx:116-127 which only shows *node* errors from the stream.
impact: If Cancel is refused (permission, already-terminal task, quota, network) the button simply does nothing and the user has no way to know the task is still running and still spending. Same for an approval that fails.
fix: Wrap each handler in try/catch, store the message in local state, and render it near the control the same way lib/api.ts callers do elsewhere (e.g. memory/page.tsx:80-91).

title: Chat, Tasks, Files, Images and Videos render and poll before the session resolves, sending a stale project id
evidence: Only ask, memory, platform, usage, settings and the task-detail loader are wrapped in RequireSession (grep for RequireSession across frontend/app). files/page.tsx:38-42 starts a 2-second poll on mount, images/page.tsx:23-29 and videos/page.tsx:22-26 do the same, tasks/page.tsx:38 fetches on mount, ChatView.tsx:32-36 fetches conversations on mount. Each goes through apiFetch, which reads `aip.selectedProjectId` straight from localStorage (auth-client.ts:41-48, 115-118). frontend/app/agent/task-detail-loader.tsx:15-19 states the rule these screens break: "fetching before the session resolves would send a stale project from a previous login — the request either 403s or, worse, names a project the user no longer belongs to."
impact: After signing out and signing in as a different user, these five screens fire requests carrying the previous account's project id until /auth/me returns; the server rejects them (no cross-tenant leak, ADR-049 scoping holds), but the user sees a raw error and the polls keep firing. An anonymous visitor also gets a fully painted screen polling every 2s before the redirect.
fix: Wrap each of these five page bodies in `<RequireSession>` exactly as ask/memory/platform/usage already do.

title: Provider honesty labels are hardcoded prose, not read from the API — a real provider is still announced as a mock
evidence: images/page.tsx:52-55 always prints "Runs on a mock provider until real image credentials are supplied ... every image below is a real, clearly-labeled placeholder SVG". videos/page.tsx:49-53 always prints "on a mock clip provider". ChatView.tsx:100 always prints "Running against whichever provider is configured (mock by default)". None of the three reads the live signal: backend/src/routes/v1/platform.ts:24-42 returns `models[].isMock`, and platform.ts:45-72 returns `providers.image.available` / `providers.video.available` / `embeddings.semantic`. backend/src/providers.ts:40-52 shows a real image provider is selected whenever IMAGE_BASE_URL + IMAGE_MODEL are set, and providers.ts:66-80 registers a real local LLM whenever LLM_BASE_URL + LLM_MODEL are set — both perfectly possible on this machine via Ollama.
impact: A deployment wired to a real local image model or Ollama still tells the user the output is a mock placeholder, which destroys the honesty signal in both directions and makes a genuine acceptance run read as fake. In production, where selectImageProvider returns null, the page still invites generation and only fails on submit.
fix: Fetch /api/v1/providers (or /api/v1/models) once per screen and derive the banner from `isMock` / `available`, so the label tracks the deployment instead of asserting a default.

title: Video scene previews are hardcoded to , which only works for the mock provider's GIF clips
evidence: videos/[id]/page.tsx:100 renders each succeeded scene as ``. backend/packages/providers/video-mock/src/index.ts:65 stores clips as `image/gif`; the real provider stores `video/mp4` (backend/packages/providers/video-replicate/src/index.test.ts:165 asserts `{ mimeType: "video/mp4", ext: "mp4" }`). The final render is correctly a `
impact: The moment a real video provider is configured, every scene thumbnail on the detail screen becomes a broken image. The screen only looks right against the mock.
fix: Choose the element from the asset's media type (or render `<video muted loop controls>` for both, which plays a GIF-derived clip fine), rather than assuming an image.

title: A video whose only failure is the final render cannot be retried from the UI
evidence: videos/[id]/page.tsx:42 computes `hasFailedScenes = scenes.some(s => s.status === "failed")` and line 53 renders the Retry button only when that is true. The endpoint handles the render case: backend/packages/media/src/video-orchestration.ts:154 explicitly resets `project.renderStatus === "failed"` so "otherwise it is a one-shot latch and the completion check below could never enqueue", and POST /api/v1/videos/:id/retry (backend/src/routes/v1/videos.ts:118) drives that orchestration.
impact: The commonest local failure — `renderStatus: "skipped_no_ffmpeg"` or `"failed"` with every scene succeeded — leaves the project permanently stuck with no control, even after ffmpeg is installed. The one button that would fix it is hidden by its own condition.
fix: Show Retry when `hasFailedScenes || project.renderStatus === "failed" || project.renderStatus === "skipped_no_ffmpeg"`, and label it 'Retry' rather than 'Retry failed scenes'.

title: Clearing a number field on the video form sends null and shows the user a raw zod issue array
evidence: videos/page.tsx:69 and :79 set state from `Number(e.target.value)`; an empty field yields NaN, which `JSON.stringify` serialises as `null`. The server then fails shared/src/video.ts:56-60 and the route throws `new ValidationError(parsed.error.message)` — the full zod issue JSON — which the page prints verbatim via `setError(String(e))` (videos/page.tsx:38). The UI also enforces no maximum on targetDurationSeconds although the schema caps it at 1800, and caps sceneClipSeconds at 8 although the schema allows 30.
impact: An empty or out-of-range duration produces a wall of JSON instead of a field-level message; the form validates nothing client-side.
fix: Guard with `Number.isFinite` before submitting, add `max={1800}` / `required`, and show the ApiError's `message` field rather than `String(e)` (which also prefixes every message with 'ApiError:').

title: An API outage is presented to the user as being signed out
evidence: session-context.tsx:77-81 catches any failure of fetchSession and sets status to "anonymous", with the comment "treat it as anonymous for routing purposes but let the screen show its own error state". No screen implements that error state: RequireSession renders only "Redirecting to sign in…" (session-context.tsx:142-144) and the effect at :88-92 redirects to /login. The login page only produces "Could not reach the server." after a submit attempt (login/page.tsx:36).
impact: With the backend down — the default first-run condition — every screen silently bounces to a sign-in form, and signing in appears to fail for no stated reason. The user is given no indication the API is unreachable.
fix: Distinguish a network failure from a 401 in refresh (fetchSession already rethrows non-401s, auth-client.ts:176-179), keep a `status: "error"` state, and render an explicit 'Cannot reach the API at <API_URL>' message instead of redirecting.

title: No dashboard or home screen; / is a bare redirect into Chat
evidence: frontend/app/page.tsx is five lines: `redirect("/chat")`. app-path-routes-manifest.json in the committed build confirms the full route set: /, /ask, /chat, /chat/[conversationId], /agent/[id], /coding/[id], /files, /images, /login, /memory, /platform, /settings, /signup, /tasks, /usage, /videos, /videos/[id]. There is no home, dashboard or overview route.
impact: The owner's journey starts at a dashboard/home. A new user lands directly in an empty chat with no orientation, no recent activity, and no entry point to the other capabilities beyond the nav bar.
fix: Add frontend/app/page.tsx as a real overview (recent conversations, recent tasks, recent generations, usage meters from GET /api/v1/usage, provider honesty from GET /api/v1/providers) rather than a redirect.

title: No error boundary anywhere under frontend/app
evidence: `find frontend/app -name error.tsx -o -name global-error.tsx -o -name not-found.tsx -o -name loading.tsx` returns nothing; the build manifest falls back to Next's builtin (`"global-error":[...builtin/global-error.js]` in .next/server/chunks/ssr/_0e1pju2._.js).
impact: Any render-time throw — including the /chat/[conversationId] failure above — surfaces as Next's raw error screen with no navigation back into the app and, in production mode, no explanation at all.
fix: Add app/error.tsx (and app/global-error.tsx) rendering the message plus a retry and a link back to /chat.

title: Almost no automated coverage of the screens: one component test total, and the browser suite never exercises a feature
evidence: The only component test under frontend/app is app/ask/page.test.tsx (3 cases about citation links). The remaining tests are library-level: lib/auth-client.test.ts, lib/chat-stream.test.ts, lib/chat-history.test.ts, lib/use-task-events.test.ts. No test renders ChatView, TasksPage, FilesPage, ImagesPage, VideosPage, VideoDetailPage, PlatformPage, SettingsPage, MemoryPage or UsagePage. The Playwright suite covers only signup/login/logout, wrong-password parity, and cross-tenant isolation (e2e/auth-and-isolation.spec.ts:26-100); it never opens a conversation, sends a chat message, uploads a file, asks a question, starts a task, or generates an image or video.
impact: The P0 above is exactly the class of defect a single browser step ("send a message, then click the conversation in the sidebar") would have caught; nothing in CI does. 'A complete browser journey with no dead buttons or undefined data' is unverified.
fix: Add a Playwright journey that signs up, chats, opens the conversation from the sidebar, uploads a document, asks a question and asserts a citation, starts a task and watches it reach a terminal state; and add render tests for each list screen against an empty and a failing response.

title: `speech` is read inside the video-scene worker closure before its `let` declaration; in ROLE=worker it is never initialized at all
evidence: backend/src/index.ts:666 `...(speech ? { speech } : {}),` sits inside the `video.generate_scene` worker handler registered at :647. The binding it reads is `let speech: SpeechProvider | null = null;` at :989. `jobQueue.start()` runs at :411, so pg-boss is already polling when :647 registers the worker. Worse, `if (!runs.http) { installGracefulShutdown(...); logger.info('worker role: no HTTP listener started'); return; }` at :768-779 returns from `main()` BEFORE :989 ever executes, and `roleRuns('worker')` is `{ http: false, workers: true }` (backend/src/role.ts:31-32). infrastructure/terraform/main.tf:424,463 deploys exactly that role as the only process that registers job workers. I reproduced the semantics with node: a closure capturing a later `let` in a scope that returns early throws `ReferenceError: Cannot access 'speech' before initialization`. The repository already documents this exact bug class for a different binding at backend/src/index.ts:769-773 ('`const mcpManager` is declared further down, after this branch returns — so the closure read a binding in its temporal dead zone and threw on every shutdown').
impact: In ROLE=worker with a video provider configured, every `video.generate_scene` job throws ReferenceError on its first line of work, burns its single retry (retryLimit 1, index.ts:435) and dead-letters — video generation is 100% broken in the deployed Cloud Run topology. In ROLE=all (local default) it is a live race: any scene job left queued from a previous run can be claimed between :647 and :989, which includes an MCP subprocess spawn (:810) and `engine.resumeAll()`.
fix: Construct the speech provider before the `if (runs.workers)` block (it depends only on `config`), or capture it through a mutable holder object the worker reads at call time, as the mcpManager case was resolved.

title: Text-to-speech is not reachable from the UI or the API in any configuration
evidence: The complete registered route surface (grep of every `"/api/..."` literal in backend/src) contains no audio or speech endpoint: /api/v1/{chat,conversations,agent,images,videos,files,memory,rag/query,usage,models,providers,tools,mcp,jobs,api-keys,assets,auth,projects,audit,admin/*} and nothing else. `ctx.speech` is consumed at exactly one site, the video-scene worker (backend/src/index.ts:666). `speechAvailable` is declared at backend/src/context.ts:87 and assigned at backend/src/index.ts:1022 and is read by no route. The frontend nav list (frontend/app/lib/app-chrome.tsx:7-21) has no audio entry and `frontend/app` has no audio page. Note: a concurrent, uncommitted in-progress implementation exists in the working tree (backend/packages/media/src/audio-generation.ts, backend/packages/media/src/speech-piper.ts, shared/src/audio.ts, backend/packages/database/src/repositories/audio-generation-repository.ts, migration 0003) but nothing in backend/src or frontend/app is wired to it, and `SPEECH_PROVIDER` (backend/src/config.ts:180) still has no `piper` value.
impact: The owner's bar 'AUDIO (TTS) generation from the UI with a provider that also works on Linux' is unmet. Audio exists only as an invisible side effect of the long-form video pipeline, and only when an undocumented env var is set.
fix: Finish the in-flight wiring: add `piper` to the SPEECH_PROVIDER enum, construct the provider in backend/src/providers.ts (not inside main()'s tail), register an `audio.generate` worker, add POST/GET /api/v1/audio, add an Audio screen and nav link, and surface `speechAvailable` on /api/v1/providers.

title: The entire SPEECH_* config group — the only switch that enables TTS — is absent from .env.example, along with MCP_SERVERS and 6 other live keys
evidence: Diffing the env keys declared in backend/src/config.ts against those present (commented or not) in .env.example yields 12 keys documented nowhere: AUTH_RATE_LIMIT_MAX, CHAT_LIVE_WINDOW_MESSAGES, CHAT_SUMMARY_MAX_PROMPT_TOKENS, COOKIE_SAMESITE, EMBEDDING_API_KEY, MCP_SERVERS, SPEECH_API_KEY, SPEECH_BASE_URL, SPEECH_MODEL, SPEECH_PROVIDER, SPEECH_VOICE, WEB_FETCH_ALLOWLIST. `grep -niE 'speech|tts|audio|mcp' .env.example` returns nothing. `SPEECH_PROVIDER` defaults to `"none"` (backend/src/config.ts:180), so the shipped default renders every long-form video silent.
impact: A user following the documented one-step setup gets a platform with narration permanently off and no way to discover the switch, and cannot configure MCP over HTTP/SSE at all — both are capabilities the owner requires to be real and exercisable.
fix: Add a classified SPEECH_* block (and MCP_SERVERS, WEB_FETCH_ALLOWLIST, COOKIE_SAMESITE, the CHAT_* tuning keys) to .env.example with the local-runtime values that work on this machine.

title: The only offline speech provider is Windows-only; there is no adapter for the Linux-capable local synthesiser that is already installed
evidence: backend/packages/media/src/speech.ts:193-195 — `if (process.platform !== "win32") throw new SpeechUnavailableError("SapiSpeechProvider requires Windows; configure an HTTP speech provider instead.")`, and `static isAvailable()` at :201 is literally `process.platform === "win32"`. The only alternative, `OpenAiSpeechProvider` (speech.ts:77-95), requires an already-running HTTP server speaking `/v1/audio/speech`. `.local-tools/piper/piper` is present on this machine (a CLI binary, verified in the machine notes to have produced a real 3.1s 22kHz WAV) and has no adapter in the committed tree.
impact: Every Linux deployment — the target of the Docker/Terraform artefacts in this repo — has no speech at all unless the operator separately stands up a TTS HTTP server. The capability advertised by the `SpeechProvider` interface is development-only on Windows.
fix: A `PiperSpeechProvider` that spawns the piper binary with text on stdin. This is exactly what the uncommitted backend/packages/media/src/speech-piper.ts already does; it needs to be committed and wired into the composition root and SPEECH_PROVIDER enum.

title: Video generation is mock-only (a 160x90 animated GIF) in every credential-free configuration, and no local real-video adapter exists although the hardware for one is present
evidence: backend/src/providers.ts:56-65 — `selectVideoProvider` returns a `ReplicateVideoProvider` only when `VIDEO_PROVIDER === "replicate" && VIDEO_API_TOKEN && VIDEO_MODEL_VERSION`; otherwise `new MockVideoProvider()` outside production and `null` in production. `MockVideoProvider` emits WIDTH=160, HEIGHT=90, FPS=6 GIF frames (backend/packages/providers/video-mock/src/index.ts:4-6, store at :65 with mimeType `image/gif`). backend/src/index.ts:524-526 logs 'VIDEO GENERATION IS MOCKED — output is an animated GIF, not video'. The only `VideoProvider` implementations in the tree are video-mock and video-replicate.
impact: Without a paid Replicate token the 'video generation' capability produces a synthetic sweeping-bar GIF, never a generated video — the owner's bar (real video validated with ffprobe) is unmet in every configuration a local user can reach.
fix: Add a local VideoProvider adapter. A real path exists on this machine and is unused: `.local-tools/sdcpp/sd-server.exe` advertises `--motion-module <path> ... enables video generation on --video-frames > 1` (AnimateDiff) in its --help, and serves `/v1/images/generations` (endpoint strings extracted from the binary), while ffmpeg 7.1 with libx264 is present to mux the frames into an mp4 the existing ffprobe path can validate.
needs_external: Replicate API token (paid) for the hosted path; the local path needs only a motion-module GGUF download, no credential.

title: docs/LOCAL_USER_ACCEPTANCE_TEST.md does not exist
evidence: `find . -iname "*ACCEPTANCE*" -not -path "*/node_modules/*"` returns no matches. docs/ contains 00..30 plus API.md, FINAL_AUDIT.md, FINAL_PROJECT_AUDIT.md, PROJECT_STATUS.md and no acceptance-test document.
impact: The named deliverable that lets an owner verify the acceptance bar end to end is absent, so nothing ties the shipped capabilities to a reproducible local walkthrough.
fix: Write docs/LOCAL_USER_ACCEPTANCE_TEST.md as a runnable, ordered checklist against the local runtimes (Ollama, sd-server, piper, ffmpeg) with the exact env values each step needs.

title: /api/v1/providers reports image and video availability without saying whether the provider is a mock, while chat and embeddings do disclose it
evidence: backend/src/routes/v1/platform.ts:69-70 returns `image: { available: ctx.imageGenerationAvailable }` and `video: { available: ctx.videoGenerationAvailable }`. Those flags are set from `imageProvider !== null` / `videoProvider !== null` (backend/src/index.ts:484 and :504), which is TRUE when the mock is selected. By contrast chat rows carry `isMock` (platform.ts:57) and embeddings carry `semantic` plus an explanatory `note` (platform.ts:62-68). `ImageProvider.isMock` (shared/src/image.ts:49) and `VideoProvider.isMock` (shared/src/video.ts:43) both exist and are never surfaced. Speech is absent from the payload entirely even though `ctx.speechAvailable` exists.
impact: Any client — including the platform screen the e2e suite asserts 'reports what is really configured, including whether a model is a mock' — reads `available: true` for a mock image/video provider and cannot distinguish it from a real one.
fix: Return `{ available, isMock, providerName }` for image and video, and add a `speech` entry driven by `ctx.speechAvailable` and the provider name.

title: The Images screen hard-codes 'Runs on a mock provider…' regardless of which provider is actually configured
evidence: frontend/app/images/page.tsx:52-55 renders the static string 'Runs on a mock provider until real image credentials are supplied (docs/26_DECISIONS.md ADR-009) — every image below is a real, clearly-labeled placeholder SVG, not a fake preview.' It is unconditional JSX. The per-generation `providerName` field is declared on the fetched type (frontend/app/lib/api.ts:76) and is never rendered anywhere on the page.
impact: Configure a real provider (IMAGE_BASE_URL/IMAGE_MODEL — e.g. the local sd-server that speaks /v1/images/generations) and the UI still tells the user every image is a labelled placeholder. The honesty banner becomes a false statement in exactly the configuration the owner requires, and there is no per-image indication of which provider produced it.
fix: Drive the banner from /api/v1/providers (once it exposes isMock) and render `g.providerName` on each card.

title: The Videos screen hard-codes 'on a mock clip provider … each scene is a real, playable animated GIF'
evidence: frontend/app/videos/page.tsx:47-52 — unconditional subtitle text naming the mock clip provider and the GIF format. There is no read of provider state; `VideoProject` (frontend/app/lib/api.ts:105-119) carries no provider field at all.
impact: Same defect as the Images screen: with VIDEO_PROVIDER=replicate configured the page asserts the output is a mock GIF when it is a real mp4, and the API exposes nothing the page could use to say otherwise.
fix: Add provider/isMock to the videos payload and render it conditionally.
