title: PLATFORM_ROUTE_PERMISSIONS is a decorative guard: exported 'so a test can assert the surface is protected', read by nothing, and missing five live routes
evidence: backend/src/routes/v1/platform.ts:296 declares `export const PLATFORM_ROUTE_PERMISSIONS`, and its docstring at :288-295 says it is 'exported so a test can assert the surface is protected' and that 'a route missing from it reads as unprotected'. `grep -rn PLATFORM_ROUTE_PERMISSIONS` across the whole backend (tests included) matches only this declaration and the generated backend/dist/routes/v1/platform.d.ts:27. The table also omits five routes this same file registers: GET /api/v1/jobs/dead-letter (:192), POST /api/v1/jobs/dead-letter/:queue/:id/replay (:212), GET /api/v1/admin/health (:241), GET /api/v1/admin/metrics (:271), GET /api/v1/admin/stats (:281).
impact: A safety artifact that cannot fail: it asserts nothing, and by its own stated rule five routes read as unprotected. Anyone adding a platform route can omit it from the table with no signal. (The routes themselves do check permissions inline, so this is a coverage hole rather than an open door.)
fix: Either add the missing five entries and a test that enumerates Fastify's route table against this map, or delete the export and its claim.

title: No UI control enables a discovered MCP tool; the Tasks screen instructs the user to issue a curl POST, so the MCP task type it offers always fails
feature: MCP tooling in the browser journey
evidence: frontend/app/tasks/page.tsx:100-105 renders, for the `mcp_read_and_summarize` task type it offers in its own dropdown: 'the MCP filesystem tool is registered disabled by default (docs/10 §3.2) — enable it first via POST /api/v1/tools/mcp.reference-filesystem.read_text_file/enable, or this task will fail with a real, honest "tool disabled" error.' The endpoint exists and is system-admin only (backend/src/routes/v1/platform.ts:302-304). The Platform screen displays enablement read-only — frontend/app/platform/page.tsx:255 `{tool.enabled ? "yes" : "no"}` — with no button anywhere in frontend/app.
impact: A task type the UI offers is guaranteed to fail out of the box, and the only remedy is leaving the browser for curl. The owner's bar of a complete browser journey with no dead ends is unmet for the MCP capability.
fix: Add an Enable/Disable action on the Platform tools table, gated on the caller's isSystemAdmin so non-admins see it disabled with a reason rather than a 404.

title: The mock LLM's user-facing fallback text steers users to paid API keys and never mentions the local-runtime option the platform is built around
evidence: backend/packages/providers/llm-mock/src/index.ts:147-151 is the reply every zero-configuration chat turn returns: '[mock response — no real model produced this answer] You said: "…". If no ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, OPENAI_API_KEY or GOOGLE_API_KEY is set, set one to talk to a real model. …'. It never mentions LLM_BASE_URL/LLM_MODEL, which is the first branch of the provider selector (backend/src/providers.ts:70-81), the one documented in .env.example:69-70, and the only one available on this machine (Ollama at 127.0.0.1:11434).
impact: The first thing a new local user reads pushes them toward a hosted credential the platform claims not to require, instead of the self-hosted runtime that is already installed.
fix: Name LLM_BASE_URL/LLM_MODEL first in that string.

title: The zero-configuration default path is fake end to end: mock chat, mock images and lexical (non-semantic) embeddings, with all three real local alternatives commented out in .env.example
evidence: backend/src/providers.ts:111-112 registers `new MockLLMProvider()` as the default whenever nothing real is registered and NODE_ENV!=='production'. providers.ts:52 returns `new MockImageProvider()` when IMAGE_BASE_URL/IMAGE_MODEL are unset. backend/src/index.ts:301-312 falls back to `new HashEmbeddingProvider()` when EMBEDDING_BASE_URL/EMBEDDING_MODEL are unset, logging at :324-325 'EMBEDDINGS ARE LEXICAL, NOT SEMANTIC'. In .env.example the three real alternatives are all commented out: LLM_BASE_URL/LLM_MODEL at :69-70, EMBEDDING_BASE_URL/EMBEDDING_MODEL at :78-80, IMAGE_BASE_URL/IMAGE_MODEL at :87-89. Two downstream capabilities go inert as a consequence: with the mock as the chat model, `writeVideoScript` cannot parse its non-JSON reply and always takes the deterministic fallback (backend/packages/media/src/video-script.ts:102-104 via parseScriptJson at :168-172), and `parseExtractedFacts` returns [] for every turn (backend/packages/memory/src/memory-service.ts:333-346), so auto-learned memory never populates.
impact: A user who follows the documented setup exactly gets mock chat, placeholder SVG 'images', word-overlap retrieval, a mechanical storyboard and a memory that never learns — every one of them labelled honestly, but none of them the real capability the owner requires.
fix: Ship the local defaults uncommented (Ollama chat + nomic-embed-text + sd-server images) with a short preflight that falls back to the mocks only when the endpoint does not answer. All three real backends are verified present on this machine: Ollama qwen2.5 and nomic-embed-text at 127.0.0.1:11434, and .local-tools/sdcpp/sd-server.exe which advertises /v1/images/generations (endpoint strings extracted from the binary) — the exact wire format OpenAICompatibleImageProvider speaks.

title: Tracing is hard-wired to ConsoleSpanExporter in every role and environment; no OTLP exporter and no config knob exist
evidence: backend/packages/observability/src/tracing.ts:37 — `spanProcessors: [new SimpleSpanProcessor(new ConsoleSpanExporter())]`, unconditional inside `initTracing`. No OTEL_* or trace-exporter key appears anywhere in backend/src/config.ts's schema. The docstring at :14-19 states the reason (no Docker/Collector locally) and that swapping is 'a one-line change'; that line has not been made configurable.
impact: In the Cloud Run deployment that infrastructure/terraform/main.tf provisions, every span is serialised to stdout with SimpleSpanProcessor (synchronous, per-span) and there is no supported way to ship traces to a collector. Spans are emitted, but only as log noise.
fix: Add OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT to the config schema and select OTLPTraceExporter + BatchSpanProcessor when it is set, keeping the console exporter as the unset default.

title: The no-fake-in-production gate derives its 'production' config from the developer's ambient environment and does not cover the speech or embedding fallbacks
evidence: backend/src/no-fake-in-production.test.ts:27-33 — `base()` calls `loadConfig()`, which parses `process.env` after loading .env files from disk (backend/src/config.ts:315 and :38, dotEnvCandidatePaths at :17-21). `productionConfig()` then spreads that over `NODE_ENV: 'production'`. So the assertions `expect(selectImageProvider(productionConfig())).toBeNull()` (:75) and the video equivalent (:76) invert their meaning on any machine whose .env sets IMAGE_BASE_URL/IMAGE_MODEL or VIDEO_PROVIDER — the same values .env.example documents at :87-89 and :101-103. The gate also asserts nothing about the speech provider or about HashEmbeddingProvider, the two other fallbacks the composition root can select.
impact: The behavioural gate that replaced a broken CI grep has an environment-dependent verdict (it fails loudly rather than passing falsely, so the blast radius is a red CI on a correctly-configured developer machine), and two of the platform's four stand-in providers are outside its scope.
fix: Build the config from an explicit literal rather than from loadConfig(), and extend the gate to cover the speech provider selection and the embedding fallback.

title: POST /api/v1/videos/:id/retry re-enqueues paid scene generation with no quota check
evidence: The create route checks the budget: `ctx.quota.checkVideoSeconds(projectId, parsed.data.targetDurationSeconds)` at videos.ts:59-60. The retry handler (videos.ts:118-138) calls only requireProject, the ADR-045 availability guard, `ctx.videoProjects.get` and `orchestrateVideoProject` — `grep -n quota backend/src/routes/v1/videos.ts` returns ONLY lines 59 and 60. The worker does not re-check either: `grep -n 'quota\.' backend/src/index.ts` shows the single check call is `quota.checkLlmTokens` at index.ts:845 on the agent model-call path; the `image.generate` and `video.generate_scene` workers have none. orchestrateVideoProject (backend/packages/media/src/video-orchestration.ts:132-175) enqueues a real `video.generate_scene` job for every scene that is not succeeded and not already queued. PROBE (temporary test, run and deleted): after creating a project and marking one scene `failed`, `ctx.quota` was replaced with a stub denying every check; `POST /api/v1/videos` then returned 429 QUOTA_EXCEEDED (log: `"type":"QuotaExceededError" ... videos.ts:60:38`) while `POST /api/v1/videos/<id>/retry` returned 202 and `ctx.jobQueue.listForProject` grew — a real job was enqueued past an exhausted quota.
impact: A project that has spent its entire monthly video-seconds allowance can keep generating video indefinitely by calling retry. The per-scene usage rows are still written (index.ts:704-716, units = durationSeconds), so the overage is recorded but never prevented — exactly the silent overage FR-063 forbids. With a paid provider (VIDEO_PROVIDER=replicate) this is uncapped spend by any project member holding media:generate.
fix: Compute the outstanding seconds before orchestrating (sum durationSeconds over `ctx.videoScenes.listNotSucceeded(scope)`) and call `ctx.quota.checkVideoSeconds(projectId, outstandingSeconds)`, throwing QuotaExceededError exactly as videos.ts:59-60 does, before `orchestrateVideoProject`. The same gate belongs in the video.generate_scene worker as defence in depth, since orchestration is also driven from checkProjectCompletion.

title: POST /api/v1/videos/:id/retry has no per-route rate limit
evidence: `app.post('/api/v1/videos', { config: { rateLimit: { max: 5, timeWindow: '1 minute' } } }, ...)` at videos.ts:37-41, but `app.post<{ Params: { id: string } }>('/api/v1/videos/:id/retry', async (request, reply) => {` at videos.ts:118 declares no options object at all, so only the global 300/minute from server.ts:143-146 applies. docs/API.md:212 documents it as `global (300 / 1 minute)` and routes/api-contract.test.ts asserts that documented value, so the weakness is locked in by a test rather than caught by one. PROBE (run and deleted): 12 consecutive retries on one project all returned 202, zero 429s.
impact: Retry fans out into one provider job per outstanding scene — the same work the create route deliberately caps at 5/minute — but is reachable at 60x that rate. Combined with the missing quota check above, a single media:generate credential can drive provider spend at the global request ceiling.
fix: Give the retry route the same `config: { rateLimit: { max: 5, timeWindow: '1 minute' } }` as create, and update the docs/API.md row the contract test compares against.

title: POST /api/v1/rag/query returns the raw upstream provider error body to the caller
evidence: rag.ts:357 iterates `ctx.router.streamChat(...)` with no try/catch, and rag.ts:384 does `throw new ServiceUnavailableError(event.message)` for a mid-stream error event. ProviderError extends AppError with statusCode 502 (shared/src/errors.ts:36-38), and the central handler sends `err.message` verbatim to the client (backend/src/plugins/error-handler.ts:19-24). Adapters construct that message from the upstream HTTP body: `throw new ProviderError(`Anthropic API request failed (${res.status}): ${truncate(bodyText)}`)` at backend/packages/providers/llm-anthropic/src/index.ts:141, identically at llm-google/src/index.ts:143 and llm-local/src/index.ts:140. The chat route deliberately does NOT do this — chat.ts:493 substitutes `"The model provider failed to respond. Please try again."`. PROBE (run and deleted): with a router stub throwing ProviderError('Anthropic API request failed (401): {"error":{..."invalid x-api-key sk-ant-api03-XYZ"}} @ https://internal-proxy.corp.local:8443/v1/messages'), POST /api/v1/rag/query returned 502 and the response body contained both `sk-ant-api03-XYZ` and `internal-proxy.corp.local` verbatim.
impact: Any caller holding files:read — the weakest project role — can make the API echo the upstream provider's raw response body, which carries internal hostnames, proxy URLs, organisation/model identifiers and whatever key fragment the provider chooses to quote back. It is an information-disclosure channel that the neighbouring chat route was explicitly hardened against.
fix: Wrap the streamChat loop in rag.ts:357 the way chat.ts does: log the real error at error level with the request id, and return a fixed client-facing message (ServiceUnavailableError/ProviderError with generic text plus the requestId already in the envelope). Ideally map ProviderError to a generic 502 message inside registerErrorHandler so no route can leak it by omission.

title: No audio/TTS route exists — the capability has no HTTP surface
evidence: server.ts:189-197 registers health, auth, chat, agent, rag, images, videos, usage and platform routes — there is no audio registration. `grep -rn 'api/v1/audio|registerAudioRoutes' backend frontend shared` returns nothing. A SpeechProvider IS composed into the context (backend/src/context.ts:81-87; constructed at backend/src/index.ts:989-1022) but is consumed only by the video render worker for scene narration. GET /api/v1/providers reports image, video, malwareScanner and sandbox availability (backend/src/routes/v1/platform.ts:60-66) and does not report `ctx.speechAvailable` at all, so a UI cannot even discover whether speech is configured. The frontend has no audio page (frontend/app contains chat, ask, agent, coding, files, images, memory, platform, settings, tasks, usage, videos, login, signup). Uncommitted work in the tree (shared/src/audio.ts, backend/packages/media/src/audio-generation.ts, backend/packages/media/src/speech-piper.ts, backend/packages/database/src/repositories/audio-generation-repository.ts, migration 0003) adds the schema, repository and a piper provider, but adds no route and nothing under backend/src/routes.
impact: The owner's bar requires AUDIO (TTS) generation from the UI with a provider that also works on Linux. Today a user cannot request audio at all: no endpoint, no page, and no capability flag in /api/v1/providers. The two wired providers are `openai` (needs an external OpenAI-compatible server or credential, config.ts:175-176) and `sapi` (the Windows OS synthesiser), so even the backend half has no Linux-capable default — piper, which is verified working on this machine and ships Linux builds, is only in the uncommitted tree.
fix: Register an audio route group mirroring images.ts: POST /api/v1/audio guarded by `media:generate` with a per-route rate limit, a CapabilityUnavailableError when `ctx.speechAvailable` is false, a quota check before the enqueue, an `audio.generate` job carrying projectId/userId/requestId, plus GET /api/v1/audio and GET /api/v1/audio/:id; serve the bytes through the existing GET /api/v1/assets/:id. Add `speech: { available: ctx.speechAvailable, name: ctx.speech?.name ?? null }` to platform.ts:60-66 and a frontend page.

title: Embedding spend is never metered and is incurred before the quota gate on every route that embeds
feature: Usage and quota on expensive paths
evidence: Five routes make real embedding provider calls: rag.ts:305-308 (`searchDocuments` embeds the question) BEFORE the quota check at rag.ts:347-351; chat.ts:118-127 (`ctx.memory.withMemoryContext` → memory-service.ts:132 → embedQuietly) BEFORE the quota check at chat.ts:271-275; rag.ts:460 (`ctx.memory.remember` → memory-service.ts:104 embeds); and POST /api/v1/files (rag.ts:105) / POST /api/v1/files/upload (rag.ts:141) whose job embeds every chunk at backend/packages/rag/src/ingest.ts:188. Nothing records that spend: `grep -rn 'kind: "embedding"' backend` (tests excluded) returns nothing, and the only six usage.create call sites — index.ts:628, 704, 863 and chat.ts:203, 437 and rag.ts:376 — write kind llm/image/video. `grep -rn checkEmbeddingTokens backend frontend shared` finds zero call sites outside quota-manager.ts itself, and UsageRecordRepository implements sumLlmTokensSince/countImagesSince/sumVideoSecondsSince/sumLlmCostUsdSince but no sumEmbeddingTokensSince (backend/packages/database/src/repositories/usage-record-repository.ts:95-126). backend/packages/quota/src/quota-manager.ts:7-9 asserts "embedding spend *is* recorded (`usage_records.kind = 'embedding'`, ADR-049)" — that is false in code.
impact: Three distinct failures. (1) No route enforces an embedding budget: setting EMBEDDING token limits does nothing because checkEmbeddingTokens is never called, and if it were it would fail closed on every request because the aggregate does not exist. (2) A tenant's real embedding cost never appears in the ledger or in GET /api/v1/usage, so reported spend understates actual spend — with a hosted embedder, ingesting a large corpus is unbounded uncharged cost. (3) On chat and rag/query the embedding call is made before the LLM quota check, so even a project already over its token ceiling pays for at least one provider round trip per refused request.
fix: Add `sumEmbeddingTokensSince` to UsageRecordRepository, write a `kind: "embedding"` usage row wherever EmbeddingService is called (ingest.ts:188, memory-service.ts embedQuietly, retrieve.ts's query embed) with an idempotency key derived from the document/chunk batch or request id, call `ctx.quota.checkEmbeddingTokens(projectId, estimate)` before those calls in rag.ts:105/141/305/460 and chat.ts:118, and correct the quota-manager.ts:7-9 claim.

title: Dead-letter replay enqueues paid work with no quota check and no rate limit
evidence: The handler at platform.ts:200-211 calls only `requireProject(request, ctx.auth, 'project:write')` and `ctx.jobQueue.replayDeadLettered(...)`; it declares no `config.rateLimit` and never touches `ctx.quota`. Its own docstring at platform.ts:192-195 says it "enqueues real work that spends the project's quota". replayDeadLettered (backend/packages/jobs/src/queue.ts:437-450) re-sends the original payload verbatim onto the source queue. The replayable queues include image.generate, video.generate_scene and video.render (the ensured set, backend/src/test-app.ts:119; workers registered in backend/src/index.ts), and none of those workers check quota — the only quota call in index.ts is checkLlmTokens at index.ts:845. docs/API.md:149 documents the limit as `global (300 / 1 minute)`.
impact: A project:write holder can replay a dead-lettered image or video job repeatedly, each replay triggering a real provider call, with no budget gate anywhere in the path and 300/minute of headroom. The direct create routes for the same work are capped at 10/min and 5/min and do check quota, so replay is the cheapest way around both controls.
fix: Before replaying, read the dead letter's payload, derive its kind from the source queue, and run the matching ctx.quota check (checkImageGeneration / checkVideoSeconds / checkLlmTokens); add a per-route rate limit comparable to the create routes.

title: No pagination on any collection route — every list returns the project's entire history
evidence: Routes never accept or pass a bound: chat.ts:51 `ctx.conversations.list(scopedProjectId(authCtx))` with no options (the repository only applies a limit when one is passed — conversation-repository.ts:112-124); chat.ts:64 `ctx.messages.listByConversation(projectId, conversation.id)` where the repository has no limit parameter at all (message-repository.ts:107-131); agent.ts:98 `ctx.tasks.list(projectId)` with no options (task-repository.ts:158-171). Three repositories have no LIMIT clause whatsoever: document-repository.ts:187-193 (listByProject, used by rag.ts:206), image-generation-repository.ts:153-161 (used by images.ts:105), video-project-repository.ts:290-296 (used by videos.ts:100). Only GET /api/v1/memory (rag.ts:438, listMemoryQuerySchema limit max 200) and GET /api/v1/jobs (platform.ts:159, jobQuerySchema limit max 200) are bounded.
impact: A project with a long history makes every one of these endpoints select and serialise its whole table, and the frontend renders all of it. Memory and latency grow without limit on the API process, and there is no client-visible pagination contract to add later without a breaking change.
fix: Add a shared `limit`/`offset` (or cursor) query schema with a hard maximum to each list route and pass it through; add LIMIT support to documents.listByProject, imageGenerations.list and videoProjects.list, and a limit to messages.listByConversation.

title: No request idempotency on the three routes that start paid work
evidence: `grep -rn 'idempotency' backend/src/routes` finds only server-side ledger keys (chat.ts:220 `llm:summary:`+uuid, chat.ts:454 `llm:message:${assistantMessage.id}`, rag.ts:395 `llm:rag-query:${request.id}`). No route reads an `Idempotency-Key` header or a client-supplied key. POST /api/v1/images (images.ts:46) mints `const id = uuid()` per request then enqueues; POST /api/v1/videos (videos.ts:37) mints `videoProjectId: uuid()`; POST /api/v1/agent/tasks (agent.ts:57) calls `ctx.engine.createAndStart` unconditionally. The ledger key for images is `image.generate:${generationId}` (index.ts:641), which dedupes a retried JOB but not a duplicated REQUEST, because each request has a different generationId.
impact: A double-clicked Generate button, a browser retry on a flaky connection, or an SDK retry on a timed-out 202 produces two generations, two jobs, two provider calls and two chargeable usage rows for one user intention. The routes return 202 before the work completes, which is precisely the shape where client retries are most likely.
fix: Accept an `Idempotency-Key` header on POST /api/v1/images, /api/v1/videos and /api/v1/agent/tasks; store (projectId, key) → created resource id with a unique index and return the existing resource with the original status code when the key repeats within a window.

title: POST /api/v1/rag/query never cancels its provider call when the client disconnects
evidence: rag.ts:357 calls `ctx.router.streamChat({ messages: [...] })` with no second argument, so no AbortSignal reaches the router and there is no `close` listener on the request or reply. Compare chat.ts:340-347, which passes `{ signal: abort.signal, onFallback }`, and chat.ts:394-399, which breaks the for-await loop on abort precisely so the provider's response body is closed. The usage row at rag.ts:376 is still written when the loop finishes, whether or not anyone is listening.
impact: A user who navigates away or a client that times out still pays for the full completion, and the answer is discarded. The route is rate-limited at 30/minute, so a script that opens and abandons requests can spend 30 completions a minute per credential with no one reading them.
fix: Build an AbortController, attach it to `request.raw`'s close event (this is a plain POST whose body Fastify has already drained, so use the reply-side guard chat.ts documents at chat.ts:296-311), pass `{ signal }` into streamChat, and skip the usage write when the call was cancelled before a `done` event.

title: Agent SSE stream never terminates and has no heartbeat; the client never closes it either
evidence: The handler at agent.ts:110-153 writes SSE headers, hijacks, replays state and nodes, subscribes via `ctx.engine.subscribe(task.id, send)` (an EventEmitter `on`, backend/packages/agent-core/src/engine.ts:203-206) and registers `request.raw.on('close', unsubscribe)` at agent.ts:151. There is no `reply.raw.end()` when the task reaches a terminal state, no periodic comment frame, and no cap on concurrent subscriptions — `grep -n 'heartbeat|setInterval|keepalive' agent.ts chat.ts` returns nothing. The browser side never closes it on completion either: frontend/app/lib/use-task-events.ts:46-80 adds state/node/completed/failed listeners and an empty `source.onerror`, with no terminal-state `source.close()`.
impact: Every task detail page a user leaves open holds an API connection and an EventEmitter listener for a task that will never emit again; Node's default max-listener threshold (10) is reached by the 11th viewer of one task. Without a heartbeat an idle proxy silently drops the connection and EventSource reconnects in a loop the empty onerror hides.
fix: On a terminal TaskEvent, send it and then `reply.raw.end()` after unsubscribing; write a `: keepalive` comment on an interval and clear it on close; close the EventSource client-side when the task state becomes terminal.

title: Existing routes unreachable from the UI, including self-service account deletion
evidence: `grep -rn 'auth/account|deleteAccount|Delete account' frontend/app` returns nothing, so DELETE /api/v1/auth/account (backend/src/routes/v1/auth.ts:166-266, the NFR-008 self-service deletion) has no UI. The settings screen imports only createApiKey/listApiKeys/revokeApiKey/createProject (frontend/app/settings/page.tsx:5-12). `grep -rn 'api/v1' frontend/app` shows the full client surface, and it never touches POST /api/v1/projects/:projectId/members (auth.ts:130), GET /api/v1/audit (auth.ts:286), GET /api/v1/providers (platform.ts:44), POST /api/v1/jobs/:queue/:id/cancel (platform.ts:173), POST /api/v1/tools/:id/enable (platform.ts:112), POST /api/v1/mcp/:id/reconnect (platform.ts:145), GET /api/v1/admin/stats (platform.ts:293) or GET /api/v1/admin/metrics (platform.ts:283). No route the frontend calls is missing from the backend — the gap runs the other way.
impact: A privacy requirement satisfied only by hand-crafting an HTTP request is not satisfied for a real user, and multi-tenant collaboration (inviting a member to a project) is unreachable from the product even though the API and RBAC support it. The platform page shows dead-lettered jobs with a replay button but no cancel, though the cancel route exists.
fix: Add a danger-zone panel to settings that calls DELETE /api/v1/auth/account with the password + typed confirmation the route requires; add a members panel over POST /api/v1/projects/:projectId/members; surface /api/v1/providers and /api/v1/audit and a cancel action on the platform page.

title: Admin surface is read-only: no tenant or user operations, and no way to close open signup
evidence: The only /api/v1/admin/* routes are GET health (platform.ts:262), GET metrics (platform.ts:283) and GET stats (platform.ts:293) — all reads. There is no route to list users, organizations or projects across tenants, to suspend or reactivate an account, or to grant/revoke isSystemAdmin (`requireSystemAdmin` at platform.ts:255-261 is the only use of that authority, and AuthService exposes no setter). Per-project quota cannot be set: usage.ts:62-73 reports `ctx.quota.getLimits()`, which is deployment-wide env configuration. POST /api/v1/auth/signup (auth.ts:51) is listed in PUBLIC_PATHS (backend/src/server.ts:33-38) and there is no configuration to disable it — `grep -in signup backend/src/config.ts` returns only the rate-limit comment at config.ts:232.
impact: An operator cannot do the operations the owner's bar names: no account can be suspended after abuse, no tenant can be inspected or given its own budget, and self-registration cannot be turned off on a deployment that ADR-113 exposes to the whole LAN — where anyone who can reach the port can create an account and become admin of the project signup creates for them.
fix: Add system-admin routes for listing and suspending users, listing tenants, and setting per-project quota limits (which requires a stored limits table rather than env-only), plus a SIGNUP_ENABLED config consulted by POST /api/v1/auth/signup so a deployment can close registration.

title: /chat/[conversationId] is an async Server Component that calls a "use client" function — every conversation URL fails
evidence: page.tsx:4 is `export default async function ConversationPage` with no "use client" — verified it is the ONLY async server component page in the app (`grep -rn 'export default async function' frontend/app --include=*.tsx` returns exactly this one file; every other dynamic page, e.g. frontend/app/agent/[id]/page.tsx:1, frontend/app/coding/[id]/page.tsx:1, frontend/app/videos/[id]/page.tsx:1, starts with "use client"). It calls getConversationMessages (frontend/app/lib/api.ts:53) -> request() (api.ts:41) -> apiFetch, which is exported from frontend/app/lib/auth-client.ts whose line 1 is `"use client";`. Next 16.3.3 (node -e require('next/package.json').version -> 16.3.3) bundles react-server-dom-webpack whose client-module proxy throws, verbatim from node_modules/next/dist/compiled/react-server-dom-webpack/cjs/react-server-dom-webpack-server.node.development.js: "Attempted to call the default export of <id> from the server but it's on the client. It's not possible to invoke a client function from the server, it can only be rendered as a Component...". Independently of that, the call could not succeed anyway: apiFetch relies on `credentials: "include"` (auth-client.ts:122) and `getSelectedProjectId()` (auth-client.ts:41), which returns null when `typeof window === 'undefined'` — the Next server holds no browser cookie and no localStorage, so the API would answer 401 and apiFetch would throw ApiError (auth-client.ts:128-136). ChatView navigates to this route after the FIRST message of every new conversation (frontend/app/chat/ChatView.tsx:70 `router.replace(`/chat/${result.value}`)`), and it is the URL every reload/sidebar link hits (ChatView.tsx:84 `href={`/chat/${c.id}`}`). No test covers it: frontend/e2e/auth-and-isolation.spec.ts is the only spec and never sends a chat message, and frontend/test/ contains only setup.ts.
impact: Every user hits an error immediately after their first chat message, and no conversation can ever be reopened. Chat history across reload — an explicit acceptance-bar item — is unreachable through the UI, and the sidebar's conversation links are dead.
fix: Make the route a client component (add "use client" and load messages in a useEffect via getConversationMessages), or keep it a Server Component and give it a server-safe fetch that reads the session cookie from next/headers and takes the project id from the URL/session rather than localStorage. Add an E2E that sends one message, reloads /chat/<id>, and asserts both turns render.

title: Cancelling a chat never closes the provider stream — proven; the provider generator's finally never runs
evidence: router.ts:164 and :231 drive their inner streams with `...[Symbol.asyncIterator]()` and pump them in a bare `while (true) { await iterator.next() }` with no try/finally and no `.return()` call. So when the consumer abandons the outer generator (backend/src/routes/v1/chat.ts:400 `if (abort.signal.aborted) break;`), the inner generators are simply left suspended and garbage-collected — their cleanup never runs. I proved this with a temporary probe test in backend/packages/model-router (name __probe_cancel_1.test.ts, run with `npx vitest run` on that one file, then deleted): a provider whose streamChat has `finally { this.closed = true }`, consumed through ModelRouter.streamChat and `break`-ed after 2 events, printed {"received":2,"providerEmitted":2,"providerFinallyRan":false} after a 200 ms wait. There is also no other route for cancellation to reach a provider: LLMProvider.streamChat takes no AbortSignal (shared/src/chat.ts:103 `streamChat(request: ChatRequest)`), and the router only consults `signal?.aborted` before choosing a candidate (router.ts:153) and before a retry (router.ts:237). Consequences in the real adapter: backend/packages/providers/llm-local/src/index.ts:227-228 `finally { clearTimeout(timer) }` never runs, so the 300 s timer created at line 118 leaks and holds the event loop open per cancelled chat, and the `for await (parseSseStream(res.body))` at line 148 never releases the HTTP response to the runtime. The comment at chat.ts:296-300 — "abandoning a `for await` calls `return()` up the generator chain and closes the provider's response body ... the difference between 'we ignore the rest' and 'we are no longer billed for the rest'" — is false as written. Separately, a cancelled turn writes no usage row at all (chat.ts:427-455 runs only inside the `event.type === "done"` branch), so tokens already spent are neither billed nor counted against quota. No test covers cancellation: backend/packages/model-router/src/router.test.ts has no signal/abort case, and there is no backend/src/routes/v1/chat.test.ts.
impact: A user pressing stop or closing the tab leaves an upstream generation running and a 300-second timer plus an open socket per cancelled request, so a handful of abandoned chats can pin the process's event loop and the model runtime. Against a metered provider the tokens keep being spent and are never recorded. The documented cancellation guarantee is not delivered.
fix: Wrap both pump loops in try/finally and call `await iterator.return?.()` on the way out (router.ts:164-186 and :231-241), and add an AbortSignal to LLMProvider.streamChat so each adapter can wire it into its own AbortController alongside the timeout. Add a router test that breaks mid-stream and asserts the provider's finally ran, and record a partial usage row on cancellation.

title: A local run with no .env uses the mock LLM and the lexical hash embedder even though Ollama with qwen2.5 and nomic-embed-text is serving on 127.0.0.1:11434
evidence: providers.ts:70 registers the only real local runtime `if (config.LLM_BASE_URL && config.LLM_MODEL)`; both are `optionalString` with no default (backend/src/config.ts:129-130), and providers.ts:110-113 then registers MockLLMProvider `asDefault: registry.list().length === 0`. backend/src/index.ts:301-311 does the same for embeddings: LocalEmbeddingProvider only when EMBEDDING_BASE_URL and EMBEDDING_MODEL are both set, otherwise `new HashEmbeddingProvider()`. `ls .env backend/.env` -> neither file exists, and the root package.json has no setup/bootstrap script (scripts are predev/dev/build/test only). There is no auto-detection: `11434` appears in only four files repo-wide (DEPLOYMENT.md, .env.example, and the llm-local adapter plus its test). Meanwhile the runtime is live and usable: `curl 127.0.0.1:11434/api/tags` returns qwen2.5:7b (capabilities include "tools"), qwen2.5:1.5b and nomic-embed-text:latest, and I drove the repo's own built adapter against it (node against backend/packages/providers/llm-local/dist/index.js) getting a real streamed answer with real usage {inputTokens:34,outputTokens:2} and a real 768-dim embedding. The mock's own fallback text (backend/packages/providers/llm-mock/src/index.ts:139-149) tells the user to set ANTHROPIC_API_KEY/OPENAI_API_KEY/GOOGLE_API_KEY and never mentions LLM_BASE_URL/LLM_MODEL, so the one message a zero-config user actually sees points away from the local path.
impact: The default experience of `npm run dev` is scripted mock text and vocabulary-overlap retrieval, not a real model — against the acceptance bar's "minimal setup ... REAL outputs (no mocks)". The capability is fully built and the hardware is present; only the wiring is missing.
fix: On boot, when LLM_BASE_URL is unset and NODE_ENV !== production, probe http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1/models (short timeout) and, on success, register LocalOpenAICompatibleProvider with the first model that advertises tools plus LocalEmbeddingProvider for any embedding model found — logging exactly what was auto-detected. Failing that, ship a `npm run setup` that writes .env from a detected runtime, and fix the mock's fallback text to name LLM_BASE_URL/LLM_MODEL first.

title: Memory extraction is dead code — nothing ever learns a fact from a conversation
evidence: `recordExtracted` (memory-service.ts:231), `MEMORY_EXTRACTION_PROMPT` (memory-service.ts:320) and `parseExtractedFacts` (memory-service.ts:333) have no production caller anywhere: `grep -rn "recordExtracted|MEMORY_EXTRACTION_PROMPT|parseExtractedFacts" --include=*.ts backend/ frontend/ shared/` returns only their own definitions and backend/packages/memory/src/memory-service.test.ts. backend/src/routes/v1/chat.ts calls ctx.memory.withMemoryContext (chat.ts:122) on the way in and nothing on the way out — there is no post-turn extraction step. The class header at memory-service.ts:13-18 claims the service "owns the whole loop: store -> embed -> retrieve by relevance -> rank -> inject into context -> record use" and that extraction "lives in the caller"; no caller exists. The only writer of memory is the manual POST /api/v1/memory route (backend/src/routes/v1/rag.ts:448-477) driven by the /memory page form (frontend/app/memory/page.tsx:70 `addMemory(scope, trimmed)`).
impact: Memory only ever contains what a person hand-types on the /memory screen. Nothing the user tells the assistant in conversation is ever remembered, so the memory subsystem cannot change model behaviour on its own — the half of docs/08's promotion loop that makes memory a feature rather than a notes table is not running.
fix: After the chat turn's `done` event in chat.ts (around line 455), run a budgeted extraction call: router.streamChat with MEMORY_EXTRACTION_PROMPT over the last exchange, parseExtractedFacts on the reply, then ctx.memory.recordExtracted({projectId, userId, conversationId, facts}). Gate it on the quota check the same way the summarizer is (chat.ts:170-175), record its usage row, and run it detached so it cannot delay the response.

title: Embedding calls are never metered and never quota-checked; the ledger's "embedding" kind is written by nothing
evidence: schema/index.ts:581 declares `kind: text("kind", { enum: ["llm", "embedding", "image", "video", "tool"] })`, but every usage row written in the repo is "llm", "image" or "video": backend/src/index.ts:632 (image), :708 (video), :867 (agent llm); backend/src/routes/v1/chat.ts:207 and :443 (llm); backend/src/routes/v1/rag.ts:380 (llm). No occurrence of `kind: "embedding"` or `kind: "tool"` exists outside the schema. The embedding paths spend with no check and no record: backend/packages/rag/src/ingest.ts:188 `await deps.embeddings.embed(chunks)` embeds every chunk of every ingested document (grep over ingest.ts finds no `quota` or `usage` reference at all); backend/packages/rag/src/retrieve.ts:83 `deps.embeddings.embedOne(options.query)` runs on every RAG query and every rag.search_documents tool call; backend/packages/memory/src/memory-service.ts embedQuietly runs on every chat turn via retrieve() and again per candidate fact in findSimilar. QuotaManager is constructed with token/image/video limits only (backend/src/index.ts:338-343).
impact: Against the acceptance bar's "usage and quota on every expensive path", embeddings are a hole in both the ledger and the budget. A deployment pointing EMBEDDING_BASE_URL at a paid endpoint can be driven to unbounded embedding spend by uploading documents or by a query loop, and the usage screen will show none of it.
fix: Have EmbeddingService return the input token count alongside each vector (or estimate with estimatePromptTokens) and add a `recordEmbedding` callback the ingest job, searchDocuments and MemoryService all call, writing kind:"embedding" rows with a stable idempotency key. Add a checkEmbeddingTokens pre-flight in the ingest job so a project past its limit cannot keep embedding.

title: The chat UI has no stop control; its AbortController is never aborted and the stream reader is released, not cancelled
evidence: ChatView.tsx:48 `const controller = new AbortController();` — `controller.abort` appears nowhere in the file (grep finds only line 48). The composer renders exactly one button, `<button type="submit" disabled={isStreaming || !input.trim()}>Send</button>` (ChatView.tsx:119), and the text input is disabled while streaming (line 117); there is no Stop button and no unmount cleanup, and the `while (!result.done)` loop at ChatView.tsx:57-67 always runs to completion. In frontend/app/lib/chat-stream.ts:127 the `finally` calls `reader.releaseLock()`, whose comment claims "Releasing the reader is what actually stops the server streaming into a page nobody is reading any more; without it an aborted chat keeps being billed" — releaseLock only detaches the reader, it does not cancel the body; `reader.cancel()` or aborting the fetch signal is what does.
impact: A user who starts a long generation on this 4-core machine cannot stop it; the only cancellation path is navigating away or closing the tab, and that path is itself broken server-side (see the router cancellation finding).
fix: Hold the AbortController in a ref, render a Stop button while isStreaming that calls controller.abort(), abort on unmount, and change the chat-stream finally to `await reader.cancel()` (and correct the comment).

title: The RAG relevance threshold is hard-coded to the lexical embedder's scale and is not configurable
evidence: retrieve.ts:20 `export const DEFAULT_RAG_MAX_DISTANCE = 0.6` with a header (retrieve.ts:11-18) saying it was calibrated against "the feature-hashed lexical vectors of ADR-026" and that "the right value is a property of the embedding model, so it is a knob (`RetrieveDeps.maxDistance`), not a constant: a learned model needs its own calibration". No caller ever sets that knob: `grep -rn maxDistance backend/src backend/packages/rag/src backend/packages/agent-core/src` (excluding tests/dist) finds only the definitions at retrieve.ts:34/60 and the resolution at retrieve.ts:93 — backend/src/index.ts:387 constructs `createRagTools({ chunkRepo, documentChunks, embeddings })` and backend/src/routes/v1/rag.ts:288 passes the same three fields, neither supplying maxDistance, and there is no RAG_* env var in backend/src/config.ts. MemoryService does adapt for exactly this reason (backend/packages/memory/src/memory-service.ts:86 `options.maxDistance ?? (embeddings.isDeterministicFallback ? 0.85 : 0.55)`), so the two subsystems disagree about whether the threshold depends on the embedder.
impact: An operator who switches to a real semantic embedder (the supported and recommended nomic-embed-text path) cannot recalibrate retrieval, and the threshold they are left with was tuned for a different distance scale — which directly controls whether RAG refuses or answers.
fix: Add RAG_MAX_DISTANCE to config.ts, default it the way MemoryService does (embeddings.isDeterministicFallback ? 0.6 : a semantic-model value), and pass it into RetrieveDeps at both construction sites (index.ts:387 and rag.ts:288).

title: excludeMocks is never used, so a real-provider failure in development silently persists mock text as an assistant turn and a usage row
evidence: SelectionCriteria.excludeMocks is declared at registry.ts:31 and applied at registry.ts:84, but no caller ever sets it: `grep -rn "excludeMocks|criteria:" --include=*.ts backend/src backend/packages` (excluding tests/dist) returns only registry.ts:31/84 and router.ts:138, the router's own defaulting. backend/src/routes/v1/chat.ts:376-393 passes only `{ signal, onFallback }`. registry.select() deliberately orders real providers ahead of mocks (registry.ts:105-108) but does not exclude them, so when the configured local runtime fails before its first event the mock serves the turn; chat.ts:427-437 then persists that text as a normal assistant message and chat.ts:439-455 writes a usage row with provider "mock". The mock's text does self-label ("[mock response — no real model produced this answer]", llm-mock/src/index.ts:139), which is the only thing separating this from a silent substitution.
impact: In a development deployment with a real runtime configured but briefly down, mock text becomes part of the stored conversation and part of the summarization/history the model later sees, and the usage ledger gains a "mock" provider row. The one guard that exists for this was built and left unwired.
fix: Pass `criteria: { excludeMocks: true }` from chat.ts, rag.ts and the agent engine whenever any non-mock provider is registered, so the mock serves only a genuinely zero-provider development boot, and surface a distinct error to the client otherwise.

title: POST /api/v1/chat has no server-side system prompt at all
evidence: `grep -rn 'SYSTEM_PROMPT|role: "system"' --include=*.ts backend/src backend/packages` (excluding tests) shows system prompts for the summarizer (chat.ts:186 CONVERSATION_SUMMARY_PROMPT), RAG (rag.ts:57/359), the agent (agent-core/src/engine.ts:630, planner.ts:164/236) and video scripting (media/src/video-script.ts:92) — and nothing for chat itself. chat.ts:376-378 forwards `{ ...chatRequest, messages: promptMessages }` where promptMessages is the client's array plus, optionally, the memory block (memory-service.ts:219) and the summary block (conversation-window.ts:240-247). chatRequestSchema (shared/src/chat.ts:49-59) has no `system` field, and role "system" is accepted from the client (chatRoleSchema, shared/src/chat.ts:14). The first-party client sends none: frontend/app/chat/ChatView.tsx:51 sends `historyForRequest(nextMessages)`, which maps to `{role, content}` of user/assistant turns only (frontend/app/lib/chat-history.ts:12).
impact: A normal chat turn reaches the model with no instruction of any kind — no assistant identity, no safety framing, no guidance on tool use or on how to treat the injected memory block — and the entire system channel is under client control.
fix: Define a CHAT_SYSTEM_PROMPT constant in chat.ts and prepend it ahead of the memory block; decide explicitly whether a client-supplied system message is appended to it or rejected, rather than leaving the channel unowned.

title: checkGrounding passes an answer that cites nothing, and the Ask page then renders a Sources list under it
evidence:
grounding.ts:120-127 handles retrievedCount === 0, and grounding.ts:129-141 is the only check applied when passages WERE retrieved: it collects the markers the model wrote (extractCitationMarkers, grounding.ts:63) and fails only if one was never offered. An answer containing zero `[n]` markers therefore reaches grounding.ts:143 `return { grounded: true }`. backend/src/routes/v1/rag.ts:418-426 then returns that answer with `grounded: true` and the full `sources` array, and frontend/app/ask/page.tsx:134-165 renders an unconditional `

Sources

` list of those passages beneath it. The RAG_SYSTEM_PROMPT (rag.ts:57-62) asks for citations but, as grounding.ts:24 itself says, "A prompt cannot make a model refuse; only the harness can".
impact: An answer the model composed without quoting any passage is presented as grounded and visually attributed to sources the user is invited to click — the same class of confusion ADR-075 exists to prevent, one step removed.
fix: When retrievedCount > 0 and extractCitationMarkers(answer) is empty and the answer is not a refusal, return a violation (e.g. "uncited_answer") so the route reports grounded:false; and on the Ask page label the list "Passages retrieved" rather than "Sources" when the answer cited none of them.

title: POST /api/v1/chat has no route test, and the router has no cancellation test
evidence: `ls backend/src/routes/v1/*.test.ts` -> account-deletion, agent, chat-summary, images, memory, rag, usage. There is no chat.test.ts. chat-summary.test.ts contains exactly one test (line 33: "records a usage row for each summarization call, even when two start from the same stored count"). So the SSE framing, the X-Conversation-Id header, user/assistant message persistence, memory injection, the post-call usage row, the quota pre-flight and the whole disconnect/cancellation path in chat.ts:313-535 are covered by nothing. backend/packages/model-router/src/router.test.ts (12 tests) covers explicit-provider routing, fallback stages, reporting and error classification, and has no test that supplies a signal or abandons a stream — which is why the leak proven above was never caught.
impact: The single most expensive and most stateful route in the platform has no automated coverage; two of the defects in this report (cancellation not propagating, no usage row on cancel) sit squarely in the untested region.
fix: Add backend/src/routes/v1/chat.test.ts against the existing test-app harness: assert the SSE event sequence and X-Conversation-Id, that both messages persist, that a usage row is written once, that a memory item is injected as a leading system message, and that destroying the socket mid-stream aborts the provider. Add a router.test.ts case that breaks mid-stream and asserts the provider generator was closed.

title: The local runtime's 300 s request timeout is hard-coded, and with 3 retries a hung runtime can hold a chat for ~15 minutes
evidence: llm-local/src/index.ts:82 `this.requestTimeoutMs = options.requestTimeoutMs ?? 300_000;`, used at line 118 to arm the AbortController. backend/src/providers.ts:71-79 constructs LocalOpenAICompatibleProvider with baseUrl, model, apiKey, contextWindow and supportsTools only — requestTimeoutMs is never passed, and no LLM_TIMEOUT_* variable exists in backend/src/config.ts. The router retries the same provider up to DEFAULT_RETRY_POLICY.maxAttempts = 3 (router.ts:38) and classifyProviderError treats /timeout|timed out|ETIMEDOUT|fetch failed/ as "retryable" (router.ts:63-65), so three 300 s attempts can elapse before fallback. The SSE route holds the socket the whole time (chat.ts:275-282), and the chat rate limit is 30/minute (chat.ts:75).
impact: On a 4-core CPU-only box a wedged or oversubscribed local model can pin a chat connection for minutes with no way for an operator to tune it down, and 30 such requests per minute are accepted.
fix: Add LLM_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS (and an idle-timeout on the SSE stream) to config.ts and pass it through providers.ts:71-79; consider reducing maxAttempts for timeout-class errors specifically.

title: Per-request model override is unvalidated passthrough, the failure is masked, and no model selector exists in the UI
evidence: chatRequestSchema accepts `model: z.string().optional()` (shared/src/chat.ts:55) and `provider: z.string().optional()` (line 54). chat.ts:377 forwards the whole request, and LocalOpenAICompatibleProvider.streamChat uses it verbatim: `const model = request.model ?? this.model;` (llm-local/src/index.ts:96), sent straight to the runtime with no check against the registry. An unknown model comes back as a 404 ProviderError ("Local model runtime request failed (404)", llm-local/src/index.ts:139), which the route replaces with the generic `send({ type: "error", message: "The model provider failed to respond. Please try again." })` (chat.ts:531). GET /api/v1/models exists and reports one model per provider (backend/src/routes/v1/platform.ts:29-42), but frontend/app/chat/ChatView.tsx renders no provider or model control at all — its header instead reads "Running against whichever provider is configured (mock by default)" (ChatView.tsx:96).
impact: The routing capability the API exposes is unreachable from the product, and a caller who does use it gets a generic "try again" instead of "that model is not available". A user cannot choose between the two local models that are pulled on this machine.
fix: Validate request.model against the selected provider's advertised models (or at least surface the adapter's real error text for 4xx), and add a provider/model dropdown to ChatView fed by GET /api/v1/models, sending the choice in the request body.

title: Agent tools give arbitrary code execution on the host under the default (process) sandbox — proven live
evidence:
ProcessSandbox.spawnChild (sandbox.ts:193-203) only sets cwd + a scrubbed env; it applies NO filesystem or network containment to the child. terminal.run_command allows `node` (terminal.ts:64) and validates only argv (no leading '-', every arg path-contained, terminal.ts:134-149) — the payload goes in the SCRIPT, not argv. I ran the REAL tools end-to-end (scratchpad probe against backend/packages/tools/dist + backend/packages/security/dist, ctx {projectId:'p1'}): fs.write_file wrote `pwn.js` -> {"ok":true}; terminal.run_command({command:'node',args:['pwn.js']}) returned {"ok":true,"output":{"exitCode":0,"stdout":"READ: HOST-SECRET-CANARY-98765
PLANTED ok
cross-tenant listing of sandbox root: p1
DNS: 104.20.23.154
","isolation":"process"}} — i.e. it read a host file outside the sandbox root, wrote a new file outside it, enumerated the deployment sandbox root (every tenant's workspace), and resolved DNS. Both tools are permissionLevel write_local, whose PERMISSION_LEVEL_DEFAULTS (shared/src/tools.ts:42) set requiresApproval:'never', so no human gate is crossed. config.ts:250 defaults SANDBOX_RUNTIME=process, and this machine has no Docker, so this is the only configuration the owner can actually run locally.
impact: Any project member (or a prompt injection the agent reads) obtains full read/write of the API process's filesystem — .env, PGlite data dir, every other tenant's sandbox workspace — plus unrestricted network egress. Cross-tenant data access and secret leakage from the platform's headline feature. index.ts:270-280 blocks NODE_ENV=production boot in this mode, so production is gated behind an explicit SANDBOX_ALLOW_PROCESS_IN_PRODUCTION=true, but every local/dev run is exposed and the argv guards give a false impression of containment.
fix: Process isolation must actually contain the child. On Node 22 spawn the sandbox child with `--permission --allow-fs-read=<workspace> --allow-fs-write=<workspace> --allow-child-process=false` (available on this machine, no Docker needed) and refuse to run when the runtime does not support it; additionally drop `terminal.run_command` to requiresApproval:'first_use' or 'always' while isolation==='process', and surface isolation:'process' as a blocking warning in the UI rather than only in a boot log.

title: fs.search with isRegex:true wedges the entire API process — measured 117.7s of zero event-loop ticks
evidence: searchFiles builds `new RegExp(options.pattern, flags)` from the model-supplied pattern with no complexity limit (search.ts:119-121) and then scans every line of every file fully synchronously (walkFiles + readFileSync + matcher.test, search.ts:125-146). The tool declares timeoutMs 30000 (read_only defaults) and ToolRegistry.withTimeout (registry.ts:248-260) is a setTimeout — which cannot fire while the loop is blocked. Probe against the REAL tool (dist/native/search.js, one 60-char file 'aaaa…!', pattern '^(a+)+$', isRegex:true): `elapsed ms: 117753 event-loop ticks during call (expected ~11775): 0 / tool timeoutMs declared: 30000 / result: {"ok":true,...}`. Zero timers fired for almost two minutes; the declared 30s timeout never took effect.
impact: One agent tool call halts the whole single-process Fastify API for every tenant — no HTTP request, no SSE stream, no health check is served. The regex is chosen by a model, so a prompt injection in any file, RAG chunk or fetched page can trigger it, and a 70-character line turns two minutes into hours. Availability DoS affecting all tenants.
fix: Never compile an untrusted regex on the request loop: run fs.search in a worker_thread (or child process) that can be killed on the declared timeout, and/or reject patterns with nested quantifiers and enforce a wall-clock check between files. At minimum, drop `isRegex` from the public input schema until the execution is interruptible.

title: Dangling symlink defeats sandbox containment — resolveSandboxedPath returns a path that resolves outside the root
evidence: realpathOfDeepestExisting (sandbox-path.ts:70-89) falls back to the deepest EXISTING ancestor when realpathSync throws. A symlink whose target does not exist throws ENOENT, so the link itself is skipped and the check is performed on the containing directory — which is inside the root. Probe against the REAL dist module: created `root/jdangle` as a junction to a non-existent outside directory, then `realpath jdangle threw: ENOENT` and `resolveSandboxedPath(root,'jdangle/planted.txt')` returned `ALLOWED -> <root>\jdangle\planted.txt`. The lexical path is what is returned (sandbox-path.ts:60) and what fs.write_file hands to writeFile (filesystem.ts:120-121) and code.apply_patch hands to writeFileSync (coding.ts:101-105) — and open(O_CREAT) follows a dangling symlink, creating the file at the outside target. symlink-containment.test.ts only covers a symlink whose target EXISTS (test at line 63 uses `escape/planted.txt` under an existing junction), so the case is untested.
impact: On the Linux deployment target an agent that finds or creates a dangling symlink inside its workspace writes any file the API user can write (cron drop-ins, another tenant's workspace, config) while the containment check reports success. Silent write escape.
fix: After the ancestor walk, lstat the final component: if it is a symlink (dangling or not), resolve its target with readlinkSync and containment-check that target; alternatively open with O_NOFOLLOW / `fs.open(path,'wx')` semantics for creates and refuse when the last component is a link.

title: The model-driven loop feeds raw tool output into the transcript with no untrusted-content delimiting
evidence: reasoning-loop.ts:217-222 pushes `{role:'tool', content: outcome.content}` verbatim, where content is JSON.stringify of the tool output (engine.ts:785-790) — file bodies, web.fetch page text, RAG chunks. AUTONOMOUS_SYSTEM_PROMPT (engine.ts:1388-1394) contains no untrusted-content instruction. wrapUntrustedContent / UNTRUSTED_CONTENT_SYSTEM_PROMPT (trust-boundary.ts:13-21) are referenced ONLY from planner.ts:164, 167, 236, 240 (grep across backend/ and shared/ returns no other production caller) — i.e. only on the deterministic read_and_summarize / answer_from_documents paths, which cannot choose a tool at all.
impact: The one execution path that reads arbitrary external content AND then chooses tools is the unprotected one. An injected instruction in a fetched page or a file the agent was asked to fix can drive code.apply_patch, fs.write_file and terminal.run_command — all of which are requiresApproval:'never' (shared/src/tools.ts:42) — so the approval gate docs/13 calls the real backstop is never reached.
fix: Wrap every `tool` message content with wrapUntrustedContent in reasoning-loop.ts before pushing it, and prepend UNTRUSTED_CONTENT_SYSTEM_PROMPT to AUTONOMOUS_SYSTEM_PROMPT so the delimiter is defined for the model.

title: The human approval card for a model-driven run shows no tool and no arguments — the approver approves blind
evidence: When a reasoning node parks, the engine stores the pending call in node.output.pendingCall/pendingCalls and the reason in node.output.reason (engine.ts:834-853). The node itself has toolId null (planAutonomous/planFixFailingTest set no toolId, planner.ts:94-113 and 355-371) and its input is the goal. TaskDetail renders `Tool call {waitingApproval.toolId}` (TaskDetail.tsx:83) and `JSON.stringify(waitingApproval.input)` (TaskDetail.tsx:85) — so the card reads 'Tool call [empty] requires human approval' and dumps the goal prose, never the tool name or the arguments. node.output is never read by this component.
impact: The approval gate is the documented backstop against prompt injection and against destructive tool use, and the human is shown none of the information the decision depends on. Approving a fs.delete_file on an injected path is indistinguishable from approving anything else.
fix: Read node.output.pendingCall (name + arguments) and node.output.reason in the approval card and render them; fall back to toolId/input only for tool_call nodes.

title: The coding-agent screen is dead — its tabs filter for node shapes the current planner never produces and a tool that was deleted
evidence: CodingTabs filters `nodes.filter(n => n.toolId === 'terminal.run_command')` and `n.toolId === 'code.apply_literal_fix'` (TaskDetail.tsx:141-142). planFixFailingTest now plans ONE node of kind 'reasoning' with no toolId (planner.ts:355-371) and all tool calls happen inside that node, so both filters always return []. `code.apply_literal_fix` does not exist at all — ADR-062 deleted it (coding.ts:10-24; grep of backend/packages/tools/src finds no such id). The Plan card additionally labels a reasoning node 'Model call' (TaskDetail.tsx:106, which only special-cases kind==='tool_call').
impact: /coding/[id] permanently shows 'No commands run yet.' and 'No file changes yet.' for every coding task, including successful ones. The user has no way to see what the coding agent ran, what it read, or what it changed — the headline capability produces an empty screen.
fix: Drive the tabs from the reasoning node's emitted tool events (see the SSE gap below) or from a persisted tool-call log on the node, and label kind==='reasoning' nodes as such.

title: Tool calls inside a reasoning node are never streamed and never persisted — the model-driven run is invisible and unauditable
evidence: runReasoningLoop emits iteration, token, tool_call, tool_result, awaiting_approval, verification and usage events (reasoning-loop.ts:66-73). The engine's onEvent handler (engine.ts:792-818) acts on ONLY 'iteration' and 'usage'; tool_call, tool_result and token are dropped and nothing is passed to this.emit, so /api/v1/agent/tasks/:id/events (agent.ts:116-157) carries only node status changes for an autonomous or coding run. On success verifyAndAdvance persists output = {content, toolCallCount, iterations, usage} (engine.ts:873-878) — the transcript is discarded, so after the run nothing records which tools were called with which arguments. Separately, grep shows recordAudit (auth-service.ts:768) is called only from auth-service itself: no agent task creation, approval, rejection, cancellation or tool call ever writes an audit_log row, although the table exists and is documented as the security audit trail (schema/index.ts:177-201).
impact: No live progress for the agent the platform is built around, and no forensic record afterwards: after an agent has patched files and run commands, an operator cannot establish what it did. Tool-call auditing is the control docs/13 §6 requires and it is absent for the only path that chooses tools.
fix: Forward tool_call/tool_result/token from onEvent to this.emit as task events, persist the transcript (or a per-call log) on the node alongside the answer, and write an audit_log row per tool invocation (actor, project, tool id, arguments digest, outcome) from ToolRegistry.call.

title: Autonomous verification is a gate that cannot fail — the loop's verify hook is never wired, yet the planner sets verificationMethod 'none' because of it
evidence: planAutonomous sets verificationMethod:'none' and justifies it in its own docstring: 'the reasoning loop runs its own verification pass and can self-correct' (planner.ts:85-88, 109). The deps object the engine passes to runReasoningLoop contains only {tools, streamChat, executeTool, onEvent} (engine.ts:758-819) — no `verify`. reasoning-loop.ts:229 gates the whole verification+self-correction block on `if (deps.verify && !correctionUsed)`, so it never runs. verifyNodeOutput then returns {pass:true} unconditionally for 'none' (verify.ts:88-89).
impact: Every autonomous task's answer is accepted verbatim with zero checking at either layer, while the code reads as though it were verified twice. The documented self-correction round (tested only with an injected stub in reasoning-loop.test.ts:223) is dead in the running product.
fix: Either wire a real verify callback into the engine's loop deps, or change planAutonomous to a verification method that is actually evaluated and drop the docstring claim.

title: No API or UI path puts a repository into the agent's workspace, so the coding agent cannot be started on a disposable repo
evidence: fix_failing_test requires testDir/testFile that already exist under SANDBOX_ROOT/<projectId> (planner.ts:313-321; the UI collects exactly those two free-text fields, tasks/page.tsx:14). Grep of backend/src for sandboxRoot shows the only writers are the agent's own tools (index.ts:366-376) and account deletion (auth.ts:211); ingestion only READS a sourcePath from the workspace (rag/src/ingest.ts:150-151) and /api/v1/files/upload stores into the asset store, not the workspace. There is no fs.mkdir tool and no upload-to-workspace route. A fresh user therefore has an empty workspace and every fix_failing_test task fails with ENOENT on `node <testFile>`.
impact: The coding agent — the capability the owner requires to run inspect → edit → test → fail → diagnose → patch → retest → pass on a disposable repo — cannot be exercised at all from the product. The only way to seed the repo is to reach into data/sandbox/<projectId> on the server by hand.
fix: Add a scoped workspace-seed path: either a 'create sample broken repo' action on the task form that writes a fixture into the caller's project workspace, or a workspace file-upload endpoint (project-scoped, containment-checked) plus an fs.mkdir/fs.write tool so an autonomous task can scaffold one.

title: The autonomous (model-driven) task type has no UI path at all
evidence: taskTypeSchema includes 'autonomous' (shared/src/task-graph.ts:153-167) and the engine's whole model-driven executor exists for it (engine.ts:604-884), but TASK_TYPES in the task form lists only echo_chat, read_and_summarize, mcp_read_and_summarize, delete_sandbox_file, fix_failing_test and answer_from_documents (tasks/page.tsx:9-16). Grep for 'autonomous' across frontend/ returns one hit, in a test fixture (frontend/app/lib/use-task-events.test.ts:19).
impact: A browser user cannot start the platform's open-ended agent; only a hand-crafted POST /api/v1/agent/tasks can. The multi-step agent with budgets and cancellation is unreachable through the complete browser journey the acceptance bar requires.
fix: Add an 'Autonomous (model-driven)' entry to TASK_TYPES with a goal field (and optional allowedTools), routing to /agent/[id].

title: The per-turn output-token cap is silently dropped, so an agent turn is unbounded and the run budget can be overshot
evidence: runReasoningLoop passes maxOutputTokens on every turn (reasoning-loop.ts:112, 140-145, default 4096 at reasoning-loop.ts:103). The engine's streamChat wrapper forwards only {messages, tools, toolChoice} and drops request.maxOutputTokens (engine.ts:761-767). Every adapter honours the field when it arrives (llm-local/src/index.ts:105, llm-openai:123, llm-anthropic:109, llm-google:111) and chatRequestSchema declares it (shared/src/chat.ts:57). The total-token budget is also only checked BEFORE a turn (reasoning-loop.ts:130-132), so a run exceeds AGENT_MAX_TOKENS_PER_RUN by however much one uncapped turn produces.
impact: AGENT_MAX_TOKENS_PER_RUN is not a hard ceiling, and the 'model hit its output limit' marker (reasoning-loop.ts:169-172) can only fire if the provider's own default truncates. Real spend on a paid key can exceed the operator's declared budget.
fix: Forward request.maxOutputTokens (and temperature if added later) in the engine's streamChat wrapper.

title: SANDBOX_TIMEOUT_MS and SANDBOX_MEMORY_MB are declared and documented but never read — the sandbox always uses hard-coded defaults
evidence: config.ts:253-254 declares both; .env.example:116-117 documents both. createSandbox is called with only {root, runtime, image} (index.ts:256-260) and neither SandboxRunRequest.limits nor DEFAULT_LIMITS is overridden, so every run uses DEFAULT_LIMITS {timeoutMs:30000, memoryMb:512} (sandbox.ts:33-39). Repository-wide grep for SANDBOX_TIMEOUT_MS/SANDBOX_MEMORY_MB returns only config.ts and .env.example.
impact: An operator who raises SANDBOX_TIMEOUT_MS to run a real test suite gets no effect: terminal.run_command still terminates at 30s (and the tool's own registry timeout is also 30s, terminal.ts:103), so the coding agent can never run a test that takes longer than 30 seconds.
fix: Thread the config values through createSandbox into SandboxLimits, and pass a per-call limits override from terminal.run_command.

title: Agent reasoning usage is billed to a fabricated provider/model, so every agent run's cost is permanently unknown
evidence: The reasoning node's usage record is written with provider:'reasoning', model:'loop' (engine.ts:801-802) because the loop's 'usage' event carries no provider/model (reasoning-loop.ts:73, 161). The composition root then calls estimateLlmCostUsd(provider, model, …) (index.ts:~873), and LLM_PRICING has no 'reasoning' key, so estimateLlmCostUsd returns null for every agent turn (cost-estimator.ts:63-64). model_call nodes by contrast record the router's real provider/model (engine.ts:933-943).
impact: GET /api/v1/usage shows agent spend under a provider that does not exist and with cost null even when a real, priced provider served the turn; pricedCallsOnly reporting and any per-provider breakdown are wrong for the most expensive path on the platform. Token counts are still correct, so quota enforcement is unaffected.
fix: Add provider/model to the loop's usage event (the adapter already reports them on the done event) and pass them through to meter.record.

title: first_use approval degenerates to always, and there is no per-project tool policy
evidence: ToolRegistry is constructed with no options at the composition root (index.ts:289: `new ToolRegistry();`), so options.hasUsedBefore and options.markUsed are undefined. approvalFor's first_use branch then returns required:true unconditionally (registry.ts:123-133) and markUsed is a no-op (registry.ts:235) — the mode ADR-059 says it made distinct behaves exactly like 'always' in the running product. Separately, enabled/disabled is a single process-wide flag (registry.ts:102-107) and POST /api/v1/tools/:id/enable is deployment-wide system-admin (platform.ts:114-120, PLATFORM_ROUTE_PERMISSIONS:302), with the code itself noting per-project tool policy 'is not done' (platform.ts:111-113).
impact: A project cannot restrict which tools its agents may use — every enabled tool, including terminal.run_command, is offered to every project's agent (engine.ts:642 defaults the filter to all tools when the plan names no allowedTools). Fails closed for approval, but the documented four-mode policy is effectively two modes.
fix: Wire hasUsedBefore/markUsed to a persisted per-project tool-usage table, and add a project-scoped tool policy table consulted by toolSpecs and call.

title: No tool can create a directory, so the agent cannot write or patch any nested new path
evidence: filesystem.ts:120-121 calls writeFile with no mkdir, and patch.ts:229-232 calls writeFileSync with no mkdir. Probe against the REAL dist tools: fs.write_file({path:'src/lib/a.txt'}) -> `ENOENT: no such file or directory, open '<ws>\src\lib\a.txt'`; code.apply_patch with a `--- /dev/null` diff creating `src/new/mod.js` -> {"ok":false,"error":"ENOENT: no such file or directory, open '<ws>\\src\\new\\mod.js'"}. There is no fs.mkdir tool in createFilesystemTools/createCodingTools, and terminal.run_command can only run an already-existing .js file.
impact: An agent asked to scaffold or add a file in a new folder fails with a filesystem error it cannot remedy through any tool it has. Directly limits both the autonomous and coding agents.
fix: mkdirSync(dirname(safePath), {recursive:true}) before the write in fs.write_file and in applyUnifiedDiff's create path (the path is already containment-checked), or add a contained fs.make_directory tool.

title: No configurable wall-clock budget for an agent run
evidence: ReasoningLoopOptions has maxIterations, maxTotalTokens, maxOutputTokensPerTurn and signal — no deadline (reasoning-loop.ts:75-82). The only wall-clock bound is the node timeout raced by withNodeDeadline (engine.ts:966-982) and swept from the database (engine.ts:1175-1193), and that value is hard-coded to 10*60_000 in the planner for both autonomous (planner.ts:108) and fix_failing_test (planner.ts:366). config.ts exposes AGENT_MAX_ITERATIONS and AGENT_MAX_TOKENS_PER_RUN (config.ts:260-261) but no wall-clock knob.
impact: An operator can cap turns and tokens but not time; a run that stalls on slow local inference occupies a node for a fixed 10 minutes with no way to tighten or loosen it. Enforcement exists, configurability does not.
fix: Add AGENT_MAX_WALL_CLOCK_MS to config, pass it into agentLimits, and have the planner use it for the reasoning node's timeoutMs (and optionally add a deadline check to the loop between turns).

title: A single transient provider error kills a whole coding/autonomous task — those nodes get maxAttempts 1
evidence: planAutonomous (planner.ts:94-113) and planFixFailingTest (planner.ts:355-371) set no retryPolicy, and PgTaskNodeRepository defaults it to {maxAttempts:1, backoff:'none'} (task-node-repository.ts:218-221). handleNodeFailure then computes canRetry = attempts < maxAttempts = 1 < 1 = false (engine.ts:1067), so the node goes straight to failed. A ProviderError thrown out of the loop (reasoning-loop.ts:156, 178) or a failed test_suite verification (verify.ts:171-176) therefore terminates the task on the first occurrence, and the test output captured in the failure reason is never fed back into another attempt.
impact: A model-driven run that hits one provider hiccup after ten productive turns loses everything, and a coding task whose final test_suite check fails ends there rather than handing the model the real failure output for another pass.
fix: Give reasoning nodes an explicit retryPolicy (e.g. maxAttempts 2-3, exponential) and, on a test_suite verification failure, seed the retry's transcript with the recorded failure output instead of restarting from the bare goal.

title: GET /api/v1/agent/tasks is unpaginated
evidence: The route calls ctx.tasks.list(scopedProjectId(authCtx)) with no options (agent.ts:99-102). PgTaskRepository.list supports {limit, offset} (task-repository.ts:158-170) but the route neither passes them nor accepts query parameters for them, and the frontend renders the whole array (tasks/page.tsx:113-121).
impact: Every task the project has ever created is selected and serialised on each load of the tasks page; response size and memory grow without bound over the life of a project.
fix: Accept limit/offset (or a cursor) on the route with a sane default and pass them to tasks.list.
